subject: Logic
title: Proof by Contradiction
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Proof by Contradiction.

hook.text: Assume the opposite of what you want to prove. If that leads to nonsense, your original claim must be true.

buildup.text: Proof by contradiction (reductio ad absurdum) assumes ¬C, then derives a contradiction, proving C.

discovery.text: Prove √2 is irrational: assume it's rational (a/b in lowest terms), and you get both a and b are even. Contradiction.

twist.text: This method is controversial in some math philosophies. Constructivists want to build truth, not just deny falsehood.

climax.text: Contradiction proofs are powerful when direct paths are blocked. They attack from the reverse direction.

punchline.text: Assume the opposite. Watch it break.

quiz.question: What does proof by contradiction assume?
